text: Charles Alfred Maguire (May 24, 1875 – October 14, 1949) served as mayor of Toronto from 1922 to 1923. Born in Toronto, he was the son of James Maguire and Elizabeth Brown. He worked at Maguie & Company and held the position of vice-president at the Hydro-Electric Railway Association before entering politics. Maguire was a member of the Orange Order in Canada. He was first elected as an alderman for Ward Three in 1909 and was reelected in 1910, 1911, 1912, 1914, 1915, 1916, and 1917. In 1912, he served as city controller for part of the year. He was reelected in 1918, 1919, 1920, and 1921. On December 21, 1921, he was elected mayor by acclamation. His mayoral program included building hydro radials, constructing a railway viaduct on the waterfront, implementing low tax rates, extending streets, and improving the city. In 1923, Robert John Fleming challenged Maguire for the mayoral position, but Maguire was reelected. He married Lillian Cusack, the daughter of Henry M. Cusack and Elizabeth Cusack of London, on February 9, 1900. He had one son, Herbert Maguire, born on April 13, 1910. This article about a mayor in Ontario is a stub.
